subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Von Neumann Architecture
description: Learn The Von Neumann Architecture in one minute.

hook.text: In 1945 von Neumann proposed a computer that stores programs and data in the same memory.

buildup.text: The design has a CPU, memory, and I/O connected by buses. Fetch, decode, execute, repeat.

discovery.text: Storing programs in memory means the computer can modify its own instructions on the fly.

twist.text: The bottleneck: CPU and memory share one bus. Data and instructions compete for bandwidth.

climax.text: Almost every general-purpose computer today still follows von Neumann's basic plan.

punchline.text: One memory, one bus, one idea — von Neumann shaped modern computing.

quiz.question: What is the von Neumann bottleneck?
options: The CPU can't process more than one instruction at a time
Data and instructions share one memory bus, limiting throughput
Memory is too slow to keep up with the CPU's clock speed
